newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES' GREG MADDUX THREE-HITS YANKEES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES' GREG MADDUX THREE-HITS YANKEES.

text.p: (Interleague games in American League parks)
Greg Maddux pitched a three-hitter and Ryan Klesko belted his second homer in as many days to lead the Atlanta Braves to their seventh victory in eight games, 2-0 over the New York Yankees Wednesday.
Maddux (11-3), who has won his last four starts, struck out eight and did not walk a batter in his first outing at Yankee Stadium since losing the decisive sixth game of the 1996 World Series.
"Holy cow, he was great," Atlanta manager Bobby Cox said.

Maddux has not walked a batter in his last five starts, covering 36 innings. Maddux threw just 86 pitches in recording his second shutout of the season and 23rd of his career. He gave up only three outfield outs while facing just 28 batters.

"I located as good as I ever had," said Maddux, who threw eight scoreless innings in New York in Game 2 of last year's World Series. "This is a good place to pitch because of the infield. You want to throw ground balls here, because the ball slows down a lot.
"I just let it go today, it didn't matter if it was the Yankees."
"He's an artist," Yankee manager Joe Torre said of Maddux. "He had such command, always got the first strike. It was a well-played series. Unfortunately, we didn't come out on the winning side."
The Braves took the final two games of the series after New York recorded a 1-0, 10-inning victory Monday. The teams combined for only seven runs in the three-game series.

In Toronto, Joe Carter's single with two out in the bottom of the 13th scored Otis Nixon with the winning run as the Blue Jays salvaged the finale of their Canadian interleague series with the Montreal Expos, 7-6.
Carter, who snapped an 0-for-16 slump with a fifth-inning homer, blooped a 3-2 pitch from Ugueth Urbina into shallow centre.
Toronto's Mike Timlin (2-0) tossed 3 1/3 scoreless innings to notch the victory in his longest relief stint in 22 months.
Carlos Delgado also homered for Toronto while David Segui and Vladimir Guerrero homered for Montreal.

In Anaheim, Eric Karros hit a solo homer off closer Troy Percival (2-4) to snap a ninth-inning tie, lifting the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 5-4 victory over the Angels, their third straight win over their "Freeway" rivals.

It was Karros's third home run in two games. He is batting .419 (13-for-31) with four homers and 11 RBI during an eight-game hitting streak. Ten of his 19 home runs this season have either tied the game or given the Dodgers the lead.

The game saw seven errors and a near brawl in the fourth when Anaheim's Tony Phillips thought starter Chan Ho Park came in too high and tight with a fastball. Both benches emptied, but no punches were thrown and there were no ejections.

In Baltimore, Jeff Reboulet's three-run double snapped a seventh-inning tie and Roberto Alomar went 3-for-3 with a homer and three RBI as the Orioles handed the Philadelphia Phillies their ninth straight loss, 10-6.
With President Clinton and acting commissioner Bud Selig in attendance, Baltimore improved to 7-2 in interleague play. The Phillies are 1-8.

In Boston, Gary Sheffield's RBI single capped a three-run third inning and Kevin Brown allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings as the Florida Marlins edged the Red Sox 3-2 in the rubber game of a three-game series.
Brown (8-5) gave up eight hits. Felix Heredia and Jay Powell combined for 1 1/3 scoreless innings before Robb Nen struck out one in a perfect ninth for his 24th save.
Boston starter Tom Gordon (5-7) took the loss.
Mike Stanley homered for Boston.
In Detroit, Damion Easley and Tony Clark hit solo homers and Melvin Nieves added a two-run shot to power the Tigers to a 9-7 victory over the New York Mets and a sweep of their three-game series.
Detroit has won six of its last seven games and pounded out 31 runs and out-homered New York 14-0 in the series. The Tigers have won four straight interleague contests after losing their first five.
At Texas, John Burkett tossed a four-hitter and Damon Buford capped a five-run fourth inning with a bases-clearing double, leading the Rangers to a 9-1 rout of the Colorado Rockies.
Burkett (6-7), who has allowed a major-league leading 160 hits, gave up one run, walked one and matched a season high with seven strikeouts in his second complete game of the year.
Texas scored five runs in the fourth against starter John Thomson (2-6) for a 5-1 lead.
